linkedin.hook: OpenAI just published how they achieve sub-300ms voice AI latency at scale. Not marketing — actual stack details.
linkedin.body:
The 4-layer breakdown: edge proximity (50ms from users), streaming everything (audio in/out + tokens), 100ms audio chunks, and models trained specifically for voice.

We've shipped 6 voice agents in 90 days. Here's what we learned:

→ Edge matters more than model size. Same model, different provider: 600ms vs 350ms latency.

→ Chunk size is tunable. 150ms for sales agents, 200ms for support. Smaller = faster, but more cutoff risk.

→ Streaming isn't optional. Non-streaming architectures add 400-800ms of dead air.

→ Model matters less than infrastructure. Latency variance between models: 50-100ms. Between providers: 200-400ms.

The one thing OpenAI didn't mention: interruption handling. That's the hardest part of production voice. Took us 2 weeks to tune Goldie's interrupt threshold to 0.5s — any lower and background noise triggers false interrupts.

VioX OS ships two voice agents (Goldie + Voice) on ElevenLabs ConvAI. Median latency: 340ms. 95th percentile: 520ms. Every deployment includes end-to-end latency evals every 6 hours.

thread:
OpenAI just published their voice AI latency stack — sub-300ms at scale. Actual infrastructure details, not marketing.

Here's what matters for anyone shipping voice agents in production:

The 4-layer stack:

1. Edge proximity (50ms from users)
2. Streaming everything (audio + tokens)
3. 100ms audio chunks
4. Models trained specifically for voice

Result: 280ms median, 450ms 95th percentile.

We've shipped 6 voice agents in 90 days. Three things we learned:

→ Edge > model size. Same model, different provider: 600ms vs 350ms.

→ Chunk size is tunable. 150ms for sales, 200ms for support.

→ Streaming isn't optional. Non-streaming adds 400-800ms of dead air.

What OpenAI didn't say:

→ Interruption handling is harder than latency
→ Latency variance kills conversion more than median
→ Their API costs 4-6x more than alternatives

We spent 2 weeks tuning Goldie's interrupt threshold. Now 0.5s of user speech triggers interrupt.

VioX OS ships two voice agents on ElevenLabs ConvAI:

→ Median latency: 340ms
→ 95th percentile: 520ms
→ End-to-end evals every 6 hours
→ Auto-failover if latency > 600ms

Every deployment logs 6 latency metrics. If you're not measuring, you're guessing.

Action for this week:

Measure your voice latency distribution. Not median — 95th percentile.

If variance > 200ms, you have an infrastructure problem.
If 95th percentile > 600ms, you have a latency problem.

Full breakdown: https://viox.ai/blog
